:::caution[IoT is not released yet]
There is no HotLoop IoT image to pull today. 4.17.0 is the latest release, and it ships the Gateway and the Edge Relay. IoT is built from the same code, with its own image, chart and Quadlet units, and arrives with the next release. Every page in this section is written from `main`, and each one says whether 4.17.0 has it.
:::

IoT is the base the other three products are built on. If the box in front of you is a Pi, a NUC in a closet, a rack of smart plugs and sensors, or one PLC on a bench, this is the one. It is the smallest image of the three full products, and it still carries everything that makes HotLoop useful: the entities, the rules, the alarms and the one write gate that nothing gets around.

A bigger product never takes anything away from it. [Edge](/edge/overview/) is IoT plus the machine layer. The [Gateway](/gateway/overview/) is Edge plus the site layer. Everything on these pages is in both of them.

## What IoT has

- **Entities and the equipment tree.** Every tag gets an entity with an id that never changes, hung on one ISA-95 tree. [Entities](/iot/entities/), [the equipment tree](/iot/equipment/).
- **Automations, blueprints, scripts and recipes.** Rules compiled when you save, and named sequences and setpoint sets that go through the write gate. [Automations](/iot/automations/), [blueprints](/iot/blueprints/), [scripts](/iot/scripts/), [recipes](/iot/recipes/).
- **Helpers, the logbook and the sun.** The values your people own, one timeline of everything that happened, and sunrise worked out on the box. [Helpers](/iot/helpers/), [logbook](/iot/logbook/), [the sun](/iot/sun/).
- **Dashboards, notifications and MCP.** Screens built per role, alarms that page a phone, and an agent that can read the plant and touch only what you armed. [Dashboards](/iot/dashboards/), [notifications](/iot/notifications/), [MCP](/iot/mcp/).
- **Every protocol driver, MQTT with discovery, and an embedded broker.** [Protocols](/iot/protocols/), [the broker](/iot/broker/), [MQTT discovery](/iot/mqtt-discovery/), [network discovery](/iot/network-discovery/).
- **UniFi, read-only,** and **history written out to your own database.** [UniFi](/iot/unifi/), [historian targets](/iot/historian-targets/).
- **Users, backups and migrations that only add.** [Authentication](/iot/authentication/), [backups](/iot/backup/), [migrations](/iot/migrations/), and [the HTTP API](/iot/api/).

[The write gate](/gateway/write-gate/) is the one page to read before a real plant sees any of this. It applies to every product.

## What it doesn't have

No OPC UA server, no Sparkplug publishing with store and forward, no fleet, no multi-site, no scheduled reports. Those aren't switched off in IoT, they aren't in the binary, so no environment variable and no bad day can turn them on. The API keeps every route anyway, and a route for something IoT doesn't have answers `404` and names the product that does.

## Databases

SQLite or PostgreSQL. The chart and the Quadlet units run PostgreSQL 16 by default, and `HOTLOOP_DB_TYPE=sqlite` puts the whole thing on a file with no database container at all. Moving to another database is a backup and a restore. [The lineup](/products/) has the table, and [Backups](/iot/backup/) has the restore.

## Installing it

Helm or Podman Quadlet, the same two ways as the rest of the lineup: [k3s and Helm](/install/helm/) and [Podman Quadlet](/install/quadlet/). Both are on `main` and wait for the next release. Boxes follow `:stable` and update themselves, and [that page](/install/auto-update/) says what happens when an update can't start.
